thesis: Docusign's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 result showed revenue of $875.7 million, up 9% year over year including about 1.3 percentage points of foreign-exchange benefit, and management raised full-year revenue, ARR and IAM-mix guidance. The weaker counter-case is that reported growth remains moderate and partly currency-assisted, but the raised company outlook and improving IAM adoption keep the net read positive. The latest filing review found no qualifying scheduled litigation event or completed governance-history event.
invalidation: Company guidance is reduced, IAM adoption fails to lift recurring growth, or billings and cash conversion deteriorate materially.

thesis: UiPath's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 result reported revenue of $410 million, up 13%, ARR of $1.938 billion, up 12%, and U.S.-GAAP operating income of $32 million, alongside higher full-year guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is gross margin compression to 80% from 82% and active shareholder litigation, but the filing shows no scheduled ruling or hearing in the next roughly 90 days and the combination of recurring growth and positive U.S.-GAAP operating income supports a positive net read. No qualifying restatement, for-cause auditor departure, or operations-linked indictment was found.
invalidation: ARR growth or net retention weakens materially, gross-margin compression persists without offsetting operating leverage, or management cuts fiscal 2027 guidance.

thesis: Fastly's confirmed Q2 2026 result showed revenue of $183.3 million, up 23%, U.S.-GAAP gross margin of 63.3%, and improved cash generation; subsequent company disclosures added a Comcast deployment, new AI-security controls, and a September 22 Investor Day. The strongest counter-evidence is the remaining U.S.-GAAP operating loss and pending securities litigation, but the disclosed hearing was vacated with no new scheduled ruling date, while the auditor change was disclosed without disagreements or reportable events, so neither meets a Phase A risk flag and the operating acceleration remains the dominant read.
invalidation: Revenue or net-retention momentum reverses, gross margins retrace materially, the Comcast deployment fails to translate into commercial usage, or litigation disclosures become materially adverse.

thesis: Caesars stockholders approved the signed Fertitta Gaming merger on September 22; the agreement provides cash consideration and now depends principally on financing, antitrust and gaming approvals. The strongest counter-evidence is closing and regulatory risk plus the recent departure of two directors, but the shareholder vote removes a major condition and the director filing did not tie the departures to operational failure. No qualifying scheduled litigation deadline or governance-history event was found, so the confirmed transaction milestone supports a positive event-driven read.
invalidation: Required financing or regulatory approvals fail, the merger agreement is terminated, or a disclosed legal development creates a material closing obstacle.

thesis: Paychex's confirmed fiscal Q1 2027 result reported revenue of $1.6305 billion, up 6%, and issuer-reported adjusted/non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.34, up 10%, while management maintained full-year guidance. The positive counter-case is margin expansion and continued PEO growth, but the company also indicated a slower roughly 4% second-quarter revenue-growth profile; that near-term deceleration better explains the high-volume selloff and supports avoiding a new entry. No actual-versus-estimate beat or miss is claimed because the calendar estimate basis was not matched to the issuer's adjusted/non-GAAP EPS.
invalidation: Organic growth reaccelerates above the near-term outlook with sustained margin expansion, or management raises full-year guidance on demonstrated demand strength.

thesis: Roivant disclosed that Immunovant's IMVT-1402 cutaneous-lupus proof-of-concept study did not achieve statistical significance on its primary endpoint and failed the company's continuation bar, so development in that indication will stop. Positive secondary trends, favorable tolerability and unchanged timelines in other indications are the strongest counter-evidence, but they do not reverse the confirmed failure of this program or the resulting pipeline concentration risk. The latest Form 10-Q reported no material legal proceedings and the research found no qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: A separate IMVT-1402 program produces replicated controlled efficacy that materially diversifies the asset's value, or the company presents new controlled CLE evidence that changes the discontinuation decision.

thesis: CarMax's elevated volume occurs ahead of its confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 earnings call on September 29, but this run found no new company-disclosed operating result that resolves demand, credit-loss or used-vehicle-margin questions. The setup is therefore technical and catalyst-pending rather than fundamentally confirmed; ordinary-course litigation disclosures and a planned executive departure were not tied to operational failure and do not qualify as risk flags. Avoid a new entry until the scheduled report supplies current evidence.
invalidation: The September 29 report shows durable unit growth, improving credit performance and margin stabilization with company guidance that confirms the improvement.

thesis: BOXX remains consistent with its disclosed objective of obtaining one-to-three-month Treasury-bill-like exposure through box-spread positions, and the near-52-week-high signal is mechanical accrual behavior rather than a company catalyst. That technical character caps conviction at low; the counter-risk is derivatives, tax, liquidity and premium/discount behavior described in the prospectus, but current official fund materials do not identify a thesis-breaking change or a qualifying issuer governance event. Continue holding the existing external reserve sleeve without treating transferred value or missing lot basis as strategy profit.
invalidation: Official holdings or disclosures show a material strategy change, persistent abnormal premium/discount or liquidity deterioration, counterparty/clearing stress, or an adverse regulatory or tax change affecting the box-spread structure.
